article.title: Report: Afghanistan ranks second worst globally in rule of law
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Dari article.
Afghanistan continues to face profound rule-of-law challenges under the Taliban’s rule, according to the independent nonprofit World Justice Project.
Afghanistan ranked 142nd out of 143 countries in the WJP’s 2026 Rule of Law Index, published in October, just ahead of Venezuela, while Denmark, Norway and Finland occupied the top three positions.
After coming to power in 2021, the Taliban suspended the Afghan constitution and dismantled much of the country’s existing legal framework.

Taliban officials initially said they would temporarily adopt the Afghan constitution of 1964 and remove the provisions they opposed; however, after five years in power, the Taliban have yet to adopt the1964 constitution or establish a new constitution.

Instead, the Islamist group governs by directives, decrees and regulations that it claims are based on its interpretation of Sharia. This has raised serious concerns among legal experts about constitutional governance, judicial independence, and the rule of law.

Mohammad Amin Zia Badakhsh, a former Afghan judge, told VOA that the Taliban suspended the constitution as they entered Kabul and, since then, have had no framework to define what the Taliban's leader, Hibatullah Akhundzada, can and cannot do.
A constitution he says is necessary because it, "establishes the legal obligations and powers of a leader [in a political system],” said Badakhsh.
The Taliban leader has issued hundreds of decrees, including those restricting the rights and freedoms of women in the country.

In August 2024, the group imposed the “Law of Propagation of Virtue and Prevention of Vice,” restricting personal freedoms and religious practices and covering aspects of everyday life such as transportation, music, shaving, celebrations, and women’s behavior and appearance in public.
Badakhsh said that in the Taliban’s governance, there is no check on the group’s power and no accountability.
“The public has no role [in their politics], nor do they consider the legitimacy derived from the public,” he added. “Therefore, there are no constraints on their power."

Constraints on government power, both constitutional and institutional, are one of the eight factors in the WJP’s Rule of Law Index. The other factors used to rank countries on the index are absence of corruption, open government, fundamental rights, order and security, regulatory enforcement, civil justice, and criminal justice.

Bashir Mobasher, the president of the Afghanistan Law and Political Science Association in exile and a postdoctoral fellow at the American University, told VOA the Taliban’s worldview of governance is not compatible with the rule of law system.

“It is because the rule of law takes shape and meaning in the form of civil government, while the Taliban are seeking to establish a totalitarian government ... based on the fact that they want to apply a divine law based on their extreme interpretation of the [Sharia] law.”
He added that the Taliban’s worldview of governance is not compatible with the rule of law system.
“Therefore, if we want the rule of law [in Afghanistan], the Taliban must relinquish power,” said Mobasher.
zh: 報告：阿富汗在法治方面位居全球倒數第二
編者註：本文翻譯自美國之音（VOA）達里語原文報導。
根據獨立非營利組織「世界正義計畫」的說法，在塔利班統治下，阿富汗仍面臨著嚴峻的法治挑戰。
在世界正義項目（WJP）於10月公布的2026年法治指數中，阿富汗在143個國家中排名第142位，僅領先委內瑞拉一位；而丹麥、挪威和芬蘭則分列前三名。
塔利班於2021年掌權後，暫停實施阿富汗憲法，並廢除了該國大部分現有的法律框架。
塔利班官員最初表示，將暫時採納1964年的阿富汗憲法，並刪除其中他們反對的條款；然而，在掌權五年後，塔利班至今仍未採納1964年憲法，也未制定新憲法。
相反地，這個伊斯蘭主義團體透過指令、法令和法規來施政，並聲稱這些都是基於其對伊斯蘭教法的詮釋。這已引起法律專家對憲政治理、司法獨立及法治的嚴重關切。
阿富汗前法官穆罕默德·阿明·齊亞·巴達克什向美國之音表示，塔利班在進入喀布爾時暫停了憲法效力，此後便缺乏任何框架來界定塔利班領導人希巴圖拉·阿洪德扎達的權限範圍。
巴達克什表示，他認為憲法是必要的，因為它「確立了（政治體系中）領導人的法律義務與權力」。
塔利班領導人已頒布數百項法令，其中包括限制該國婦女權利與自由的法令。
2024年8月，該組織頒布了《宣揚美德與防止惡行法》，限制個人自由與宗教活動，並規範了日常生活中的各個層面，例如交通、音樂、剃鬚、慶典活動，以及女性在公共場所的行為與儀容。
巴達克什表示，在塔利班的統治下，該組織的權力不受制衡，也無須承擔任何責任。
「公眾在他們的政治中毫無角色，他們也不認為自己的正當性源自公眾，」他補充道。「因此，他們的權力毫無約束。」
對政府權力的限制——無論是憲法層面還是制度層面——是世界正義項目（WJP）法治指數中的八大因素之一。該指數用於對各國進行排名的其他因素包括：無貪腐、政府透明度、基本權利、秩序與安全、法規執行、民事司法及刑事司法。
流亡中的阿富汗法律與政治科學協會主席、美國大學博士後研究員巴希爾·莫巴舍爾（Bashir Mobasher）向美國之音表示，塔利班的治理世界觀與法治體系不相容。
「這是因為法治是在民選政府的形式下成形並展現其意義，而塔利班則企圖建立一個極權政府……這源於他們想要依據對[伊斯蘭教法]的極端詮釋，來實施神授法。」
他補充說，塔利班的治理世界觀與法治體系不相容。
「因此，如果我們希望[阿富汗]實現法治，塔利班就必須交出權力，」莫巴舍表示。
